items.claim: 2026 CapEx guidance updated to a $2B-$3B range, down sharply from $4.6B spent in 2025 as 300mm capacity buildout nears completion.
items.quote: the range of $2 billion to $3 billion
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Management reiterated the 2026 free cash flow per share target of over $8, based on current revenue consensus.
items.quote: more than $8 per share of free cash flow in 2026
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: 2025 free cash flow per share was $3.23, up 97% year-over-year as end-market recovery began.
items.quote: free cash flow was $3.23 per share, an increase of 97%
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: 2025 CapEx of $4.6 billion represented 26% of revenue, a level management is now bringing down as capacity investments mature.
items.quote: CapEx was $4.6 billion or 26% of revenue.
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: 2026 depreciation guidance is $2.2B-$2.4B (midpoint $2.3B, up ~$400M from 2025's $1.9B), with further but slower increases expected in 2027.
items.quote: we expect $2.2 billion to $2.4 billion
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: 2025 operating cash flow was $7.2 billion, up about 13% year-over-year as end markets began to recover.
items.quote: operating cash flow in 2025 was $7.2 billion
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: TI updated its long-term inventory days target to a 150-250 day range to preserve customer service and lead-time stability.
items.quote: inventory days target to 150 to 250 days
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: The Silicon Labs acquisition will be funded through a combination of cash on hand and debt financing arranged before closing.
items.quote: cash on hand as well as debt financing
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: TI has reduced its shares outstanding by 47% since 2004 through buybacks.
items.quote: We have reduced shares outstanding 47% since 2004.
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Over the last 10 years TI has returned 130% of free cash flow to shareholders, with returns compounding at 13% since 2004.
items.quote: returned a total of 130% of free cash flow
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: Management's long-term CapEx modeling framework: multiply the long-term revenue growth rate by 1.2x to estimate gross CapEx as a percent of revenue (e.g., 10% growth implies ~12% CapEx/revenue), before ITC benefits.
items.quote: multiply that times 1.2 to get your CapEx
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: TI received about $670 million in CHIPS Act cash benefits in 2025 (primarily ITC, plus some direct funding grants), with ITC now at 35% (up from 25%) and up to $1.6 billion in direct funding still to be captured.
items.quote: we received cash benefits of about $670 million
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: TI has raised its dividend for 22 consecutive years, including a 4% increase in Q4 2025, with 8%/15% 5-year/10-year CAGRs.
items.quote: consecutive years, we have steadily increased our dividend
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: M&A financial hurdle is unchanged: the deal must be accretive to TI's ~10% cost of capital, achieved within three to five years post-close, which management says is the case for Silicon Labs.
items.quote: accretive to cost of capital
items.speaker: Rafael Lizardi

items.claim: TI's products will play a role in the long-term industry transition to 800-volt DC data center architectures, with its GaN technology enabling higher power density per rack.
items.quote: our GaN technology will drive higher power density per rack
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: TI's embedded processing portfolio release cadence is now 6x what it was six years ago, feeding more attach opportunities for analog/power parts around the embedded socket.
items.quote: we are now at a 6x rate versus six years ago
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: Management cited Silicon Labs' strong market position — 85% share in industrial across many end equipment categories — as part of the strategic rationale for the acquisition.
items.quote: 85% in industrial across many, many end equipment
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: TI calls directly on fewer than 2,000 customers but has about 200,000 other customers it never sees directly, which is a stated rationale for investing in AI-driven ti.com/product-recommender tools.
items.quote: we call directly on less than 2,000 customers
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: Management stated the industrial end market is still running about 25% below its prior peak, framed as the biggest unknown/opportunity for 2026.
items.quote: We are still trending about 25% from the peak
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

items.claim: Management described the post-COVID semiconductor inventory correction as historically large and prolonged, contributing to the current recovery being more gradual than prior cycles.
items.quote: We saw a very large and prolonged inventory correction
items.speaker: Haviv Ilan

qa_flags.question: Under what circumstances would TI want to run at the higher end of the newly widened inventory-days range, given the CFO previously indicated wanting to bring factory loadings down?
qa_flags.response_pattern: CFO first corrects the analyst's premise (says the prior comment was from two quarters ago, not the last call, and that last call management said it was comfortable with inventory), then answers only at a high level of generality — tying inventory days to where the company is in the cycle (upturn/downturn/peak/trough) rather than giving a specific circumstance, trigger, or number.

qa_flags.question: Conceptually, if sales grow 10% this year and 10% again in 2027, what would CapEx be for 2027?
qa_flags.response_pattern: CEO gives a directional comment (likely similar to or below the ~$2 billion 2026 level) but explicitly declines to commit to a number, stating it would have to be left for next year's discussion.

qa_flags.question: How do potential M&A deals enter TI's strategic funnel, and specifically how did the Silicon Labs deal come about after it was reportedly triggered by another company's bid?
qa_flags.response_pattern: CEO explicitly declines to address the specific circumstances of how the deal originated ('I don't want to comment about that'), deferring disclosure to Silicon Labs and instead redirecting the answer toward general asset-quality and financial-fit rationale.
